lessonTitle: Leukaemia, Lymphoma and the Coagulation Screen

blocks.text: A 6-year-old boy's knee swells after a minor fall and the joint is hot and tense. A routine bleeding test shows a prolonged APTT but a normal PT and platelet count. In another clinic, a 70-year-old man has a white cell count of 60 x 10^9/L and feels completely well. Blood tests tell you whether a bleed is in the clotting factors, and whether a high white count is dangerous or indolent.

blocks.markdown: Blood cells arise from haematopoietic stem cells in the marrow and divide into myeloid and lymphoid lineages. **Leukaemia** is malignant proliferation of marrow-derived white cell precursors, usually with abnormal cells in the blood. **Lymphoma** is malignancy of lymphocytes arising mainly in lymph nodes and other lymphoid tissue. **Coagulation disorders** are failures of clot formation; the laboratory coagulation screen is a set of timed assays that tell you which part of the clotting cascade is failing.

rows: Blasts 20% or more of marrow; anaemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia; Auer rods
Rapid onset: infection, bleeding, fatigue over days to weeks
Lymphoblasts 20% or more of marrow; cytopenias
Very high WCC with all stages of myeloid maturation; BCR-ABL (Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22))
Splenomegaly; treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib
Sustained lymphocytosis (above 5 x 10^9/L) of mature small lymphocytes; smear cells
Often found incidentally; indolent, treated only when symptomatic
blocks.caption: Acute versus chronic leukaemias.

blocks.title: Acute versus chronic
blocks.text: Acute leukaemias are blast-cell diseases that crowd out normal marrow, so they present within weeks with failure of all lines: anaemia, infection and bleeding. Chronic leukaemias involve more mature cells, progress slowly over years and often present as an incidental high white count or splenomegaly.

blocks.caption: Absolute count in 10^9/L, used to detect lymphocytosis.

blocks.title: Is this lymphocytosis?
blocks.prompt: A well 72-year-old man has WCC 60 x 10^9/L with 80% small mature lymphocytes and smear cells on the film. Calculate the lymphocyte count and interpret it.

steps.text: 48 is far above 5 x 10^9/L, so there is a sustained lymphocytosis of mature small cells.
In an older asymptomatic patient this is typical of CLL; flow cytometry confirms the clone. Observation is usual unless symptoms or marrow failure develop.

blocks.answer: Lymphocyte count 48 x 10^9/L: CLL pattern, usually observed if well.

blocks.markdown: **Lymphoma.** Typical presentation is painless, rubbery lymphadenopathy (often cervical), sometimes with **B symptoms**: fever, drenching night sweats and weight loss of more than 10% in 6 months. Hodgkin lymphoma is characterised by Reed-Sternberg cells in a mixed inflammatory background, tends to spread to contiguous nodal groups, and can cause pain in involved nodes after alcohol. Non-Hodgkin lymphomas are a diverse group arising from B or T cells. **Diagnosis needs an excision (or core) biopsy** of the lymph node, not fine needle aspiration, because node architecture and immunophenotype are needed to classify the lymphoma. Staging (Ann Arbor) uses CT or PET-CT, and bone marrow assessment where indicated, and records the number and distribution of nodal groups, whether disease is on both sides of the diaphragm, extranodal involvement and B symptoms.

rows: Extrinsic and common (factor VII; also II, V, X, fibrinogen)
Warfarin, liver disease, vitamin K deficiency, DIC
Intrinsic and common (VIII, IX, XI, XII; also II, V, X, fibrinogen)
Haemophilia A or B, unfractionated heparin, DIC, severe liver disease
Low in marrow failure, DIC, hypersplenism, immune thrombocytopenia
Low fibrinogen and high D-dimer in DIC
blocks.caption: Coagulation screen: what each test measures.
International normalised ratio; ISI is the reagent's international sensitivity index.

blocks.title: Calculating the INR
blocks.prompt: A patient on warfarin has PT 24 s. The laboratory mean normal PT is 12 s and the ISI is 1.0. Calculate the INR.

steps.text: Form the ratio of patient to mean normal PT.
Raise to the power of ISI (1.0), which leaves the ratio unchanged.
An INR of 2.0 lies within the usual target range for many indications (commonly 2.0 to 3.0; target depends on indication).

items: Haemophilia A (factor VIII) and B (factor IX): X-linked, deep bleeding into joints and muscles; APTT prolonged, PT and platelets normal, specific factor assay low.
Warfarin: inhibits vitamin K-dependent factors (II, VII, IX, X); PT/INR is prolonged first because factor VII has the shortest half-life.
Heparin: prolongs the APTT (unfractionated heparin); direct oral anticoagulants may prolong PT or APTT variably and are not monitored with these tests.
Liver disease: reduced synthesis of clotting factors prolongs PT (and later APTT), with low fibrinogen in advanced disease and low platelets from hypersplenism and reduced thrombopoietin.
DIC: consumption of platelets and factors gives low platelets, prolonged PT and APTT, low fibrinogen and high D-dimer.

blocks.title: Reading a coagulation screen
blocks.prompt: A 55-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has PT 22 s (normal 11 to 14), APTT 44 s (normal 26 to 37), platelets 70 x 10^9/L. He is not on anticoagulants. What explains this?

steps.text: PT is prolonged more than the APTT: this points to reduced synthesis of factor VII and other vitamin K-dependent factors by the liver.
Platelets are low, consistent with hypersplenism from portal hypertension.
No anticoagulant or DIC picture is suggested; check fibrinogen to be sure. Vitamin K may correct part of the PT if deficiency contributes.

blocks.answer: Coagulopathy of liver disease with hypersplenism.

points: Acute leukaemia causes rapid marrow failure with 20% or more blasts; chronic leukaemias are more indolent and found incidentally.
CML is defined by BCR-ABL (Philadelphia chromosome) and treated with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor; CLL is a lymphocytosis of mature cells in older patients.
Lymphoma presents as painless lymphadenopathy with or without B symptoms and requires excision biopsy; staging uses imaging.
PT reflects the extrinsic pathway and warfarin; APTT reflects the intrinsic pathway and heparin and haemophilia; liver disease prolongs PT first.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman has a 10-day history of fatigue, fever and gum bleeding. Blood count shows WCC 2.1, Hb 70 g/L, platelets 25 x 10^9/L, and the film shows 45% blasts, some with Auer rods. What is the diagnosis?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: blasts over 20% with Auer rods and failure of all three lines.
distractorRationale.b: CLL shows mature lymphocytosis and is usually indolent.
distractorRationale.c: CML shows a high WCC with all stages of myeloid maturation.
distractorRationale.d: Iron deficiency does not cause blasts or pancytopenia.

questions.explanation: Pancytopenia with circulating blasts and Auer rods, developing over days to weeks, is the pattern of acute myeloid leukaemia. Marrow failure explains the anaemia, infection and bleeding.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man is found incidentally to have WCC 58 x 10^9/L, 88% small mature lymphocytes and smear cells, with normal Hb and platelets and no symptoms. What is the most appropriate approach?

options.text: Confirm with flow cytometry and observe if asymptomatic

questions.correctOptionText: Confirm with flow cytometry and observe if asymptomatic

distractorRationale.a: Correct: CLL is often managed by watchful waiting until symptoms or marrow failure appear.
distractorRationale.b: Intensive induction is for acute leukaemia.
distractorRationale.c: Imatinib targets BCR-ABL in CML, not CLL.

questions.explanation: A sustained lymphocytosis of mature small lymphocytes with smear cells in an older, well patient is CLL. Early treatment does not improve survival in asymptomatic disease, so observation is standard.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old has fatigue, left upper quadrant discomfort, massive splenomegaly and WCC 190 x 10^9/L with neutrophils, myelocytes and basophils on the film. Cytogenetics will most likely show which abnormality?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: the Philadelphia chromosome characterises CML.
distractorRationale.b: Auer rods are seen in AML blasts.
distractorRationale.c: Reed-Sternberg cells are seen in Hodgkin lymphoma.
distractorRationale.d: Factor VIII deficiency is haemophilia A.

questions.explanation: A very high white count with the whole spectrum of myeloid maturation and splenomegaly is typical of chronic myeloid leukaemia, defined by the BCR-ABL fusion gene. It is treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old has a painless 3 cm cervical lymph node, drenching night sweats and 12% weight loss over 5 months. What is the most appropriate diagnostic step?

options.text: Reassurance and review in a year

distractorRationale.a: Correct: architecture and immunophenotype are needed to diagnose and classify lymphoma.
distractorRationale.b: FNA does not provide architecture and is inadequate.
distractorRationale.d: B symptoms with a node need prompt investigation.

questions.explanation: Painless lymphadenopathy with B symptoms suggests lymphoma. Diagnosis requires a node biopsy, preferably excisional, because the histological pattern and immunophenotype determine type, and CT or PET then stages the disease.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old male rugby player develops a swollen, painful elbow after a tackle. His maternal uncle also bled easily. APTT is 70 s (normal 26 to 37); PT, fibrinogen and platelet count are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: isolated prolonged APTT with haemarthrosis and an X-linked family pattern.
distractorRationale.c: ITP has a low platelet count.
distractorRationale.d: Vitamin K deficiency prolongs the PT.

questions.explanation: An isolated prolonged APTT with normal PT, fibrinogen and platelets, a joint bleed and an affected maternal uncle indicate X-linked deficiency of factor VIII or IX. Specific factor assays distinguish haemophilia A from B.

questions.stem: A patient on warfarin has a PT of 33 s. The laboratory mean normal PT is 11 s and the ISI of the reagent is 1.0. Calculate the INR.
questions.explanation: INR = (33 / 11)^1.0 = 3.0. This is at the upper end of or above typical target ranges for many indications, so the dose and any interacting drugs would be reviewed.

questions.stem: A patient has a white cell count of 72 x 10^9/L of which 75% are lymphocytes. Calculate the absolute lymphocyte count in x 10^9/L.
questions.explanation: Absolute count = 72 x 0.75 = 54 x 10^9/L. This is well above the 5 x 10^9/L threshold, so there is a marked lymphocytosis for which flow cytometry would identify a clonal population.

questions.stem: Describe the typical presentation of lymphoma, the role of biopsy in diagnosis and how staging is performed.
markingGuide: B symptoms: fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss over 10%
Possible splenomegaly, extranodal disease, pruritus or alcohol-induced pain in Hodgkin lymphoma
Excision or core biopsy needed for histology and immunophenotype
Staging by CT or PET-CT with Ann Arbor stage and B symptom designation
questions.explanation: Biopsy establishes the diagnosis and the lymphoma subtype, which dictate treatment. Staging then documents extent, because stage and B symptoms determine prognosis and therapy.

questions.stem: Explain how PT, APTT and platelet count differ in warfarin therapy, haemophilia A and advanced liver disease, and why.
markingGuide: Warfarin: inhibits vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, X; PT and INR prolonged first, platelets normal
Haemophilia A: factor VIII deficiency; isolated prolonged APTT, normal PT, normal platelets
Liver disease: reduced synthesis of clotting factors; PT prolonged, APTT later, low fibrinogen in advanced disease
Low platelets in cirrhosis due to hypersplenism and reduced thrombopoietin
PT tests extrinsic and common pathways; APTT intrinsic and common
Factor VII has the shortest half-life, so PT changes first
questions.explanation: The pattern of abnormal tests identifies which part of the cascade is failing. Warfarin and liver disease both impair vitamin K-dependent factors, so PT is affected first, while haemophilia A removes an intrinsic factor and only the APTT rises.

questions.stem: True or false: fine needle aspiration alone is the preferred method to diagnose and classify suspected lymphoma because lymph node architecture is not needed.
questions.explanation: Lymphoma classification depends on node architecture and immunophenotype, which FNA cannot provide. Excisional or core biopsy is therefore preferred.
